reviewType: independent artifact and source inspection; no live rerun

integrity.note: Frames 020 and 021 contain identical pixels under different observation IDs; a fresh observation need not contain changed pixels.

supportedObservations: The owned fixture shows text input, counter increments, a checked option and the ctrl+d chord label.
Frame 011 shows later scroll rows than frame 010; frame 012 shows the drag target moved.
Frames 016 and 017 show a separately captured child window and its changed confirmation button.
Frame 014 shows count 3 after the low-level interruption/release sequence; the final frame shows count 5.
limits: Text is clipped in the visible input field; the screenshot alone does not establish its complete string.
Pixels alone do not prove process exit, input release, lease handoff, window identity or the cause of a state transition.
The retained original source and receipt must accompany the frames when assessing those assertions.

sourceProvenance.reason: The original receipt records fixture source hashes but no tested source commit or complete execution-source manifest. The run occurred before the implementation commit was created. Inspection of the later PR head must not be reported as proof that that commit was executed.

acceptanceAssessment.supportedSubset: The real MCP run delivered ctrl+d, one downward wheel action and a drag; fixture state and visible changes support those limited outcomes.
acceptanceAssessment.remaining: The complete named case was not exercised: no upward wheel action, exact scroll-position assertion, exact drag endpoint assertion or drop-count assertion was recorded.
acceptanceAssessment.oracleDefect: The original fixture reports a cumulative maximum scroll displacement. Its scrollY cannot decrease on reverse scrolling and is not a valid current-position oracle. The harness accepts scroll and drag with lower-bound thresholds.

acceptanceAssessment.supportedSubset: A directly started native held drag was cancelled. The source-owned release-left bridge reported that it released a previously held left button, followed by a successful fixture click.
acceptanceAssessment.remaining: This path calls runProcess directly with a manually supplied recovery callback, bypassing the MCP action and controller recovery path. Required MCP cancellation, timeout, disconnect, server-crash and failed-cleanup quarantine cases were not exercised live. The original summary does not retain the owned native process identity and independently checked exit/input-state evidence required for full recovery acceptance.

acceptanceAssessment.supportedSubset: A separately selected owned child window was observed and its confirmation button was clicked.
acceptanceAssessment.remaining: The fixture opens the child with Show(owner), which is modeless. It does not prove modal parent blocking. The harness does not attempt and verify rejection of parent input while a modal dialog is active; it closes the child through the fixture command channel.

acceptanceAssessment.supportedSubset: Source and retained results support old-observation rejection after move and minimize, unchanged fixture count on rejection, fresh observation and exactly one subsequent counter increment. The minimized window was restored during observation.
acceptanceAssessment.remaining: Functional checks are reusable, but the original receipt lacks the tested source commit and named-case expected/actual record required by the completion contract. Preserve this as legacy evidence rather than retroactively declaring the complete contract satisfied.

acceptanceAssessment.supportedSubset: The run records one 2880x1800 display at 144 DPI and matching PNG dimensions.
acceptanceAssessment.remaining: A second DPI scale and monitor transition were unavailable and were not tested. Recording the existing configuration does not satisfy transition acceptance.

claimCorrections: The original result passed describes its narrower script assertions; it does not establish completion of all named alpha.3 acceptance cases.
Keep the successful owned-fixture actions and existing display limits, but label modal and end-to-end recovery coverage as pending.
Named-pipe ownership release after process termination and mocked cleanup tests do not establish physical input cleanup following a TRACE server crash.
A published version, actual model-host workflow, REPLAY workflow and release readiness are not established by these artifacts.
